items.text: This emergency procedures checklist is intended to supplement the information contained in the Pilot’s Operating Handbook (POH) and serve as a handy inflight reference and instructional tool. Whenever time permits in an emergency situation, pilots should make use of all sources of information including the expanded text in the POH.
In any emergency situation the pilot’s priorities should be 1. Maintain aircraft control. 2. Analyze the situation. 3. Take corrective action.

Items in Bold Print are time critical steps that should be committed to memory so that they can be accomplished without referring to the checklist. As time permits during the handling of an emergency the pilot should then use the checklist to confirm that all Bold Print items have been accomplished.

“Land as soon as practicable” as used in this checklist means that the pilot should land at the nearest airfield that has a suitable runway (length, type surface, etc.) and weather appropriate for the pilot’s proficiency and the type aircraft flown.

sections.title: ENGINE FAILURE / POWER LOSS DURING FLIGHT (RESTART PROCEDURE)
sections.condition: Engine failure or power loss during flight

items.response: Check R, L, BOTH Positions (START if Prop is Stopped)

items.text: If Engine Power is Not Restored
Execute EMERGENCY LANDING WITHOUT ENGINE POWER
* If engine failure was caused by fuel exhaustion, power will not be restored after tanks are switched until empty fuel lines are filled, which may require up to ten seconds.
Squawk 7700 and Make a MAYDAY Call if Time Permits
Squawk 7700 and Make a MAYDAY Call if Time Permits
Conserve Altitude Until Landing is Assured
Squawk 7700 and Make a MAYDAY Call if Time Permits
* If engine power is not available, approach at 100 MIAS with flaps up or 90 MIAS with 10° flaps

sections.title: ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND
sections.condition: Engine fire during start on ground

items.text: If Fire Continues or Engine Fails to Start
Abandon Aircraft and Use Fire Extinguisher

sections.phase_label: ENGINE FIRE DURING START ON GROUND

items.text: Abandon Aircraft and Use Fire Extinguisher
Execute EMERGENCY LANDING WITHOUT ENGINE POWER
Slip to Keep Flames Away From Fuel Tanks and Cabin
If Fire is Out and Electrical Power is Required for Flight

sections.title: CABIN OR ELECTRICAL FIRE IN FLIGHT
sections.condition: Cabin or electrical fire in flight

items.text: If Fire Appears Out and Electrical Power is Necessary for Continued Flight
Use caution when discharging fire extinguisher. HALON is extremely toxic. After discharging an extinguisher within a closed cabin, ventilate the cabin.

sections.condition: Low oil pressure with normal oil temperature

items.text: Conserve Altitude Until Landing is Assured

sections.title: ZERO OIL PRESSURE WITH HIGH OIL TEMPERATURE (Engine Failure is Imminent)
sections.condition: Zero oil pressure with high oil temperature

items.text: Execute PRECAUTIONARY LANDING WITH ENGINE POWER
Confirm by Activating Landing Light or Other Equipment
* Allow circuit breaker to cool 3 minutes before resetting
NOTE: If the battery discharges completely, the gear must be lowered using the emergency landing gear extension procedure and the landing gear position lights will be inoperative.
DO NOT try to Recycle the Gear
Gear Pump & Indicator Lights Circuit Breakers
If Gear Still Fails to Extend **

items.response: EMERGENCY DOWN and Hold Until Gear Lock Down

items.text: If Gear Still Fails to Extend **
* Allow circuit breaker to cool 3 minutes before resetting
** If electrical power has been lost the landing gear position indicator lights will be inoperative.

sections.title: FOR ALL LANDINGS WITH A GEAR MALFUNCTION

items.text: Reduce Fuel Load to a Minimum
Divert to a Field With Adequate Crash Response

sections.title: LANDING WITH ONLY ONE MAIN GEAR EXTENDED

items.text: Land With Crosswind on the Side of the Extended Gear
At Touchdown or When Landing is Assured
Hold Nose Wheel Off as Long as Possible

sections.title: LANDING WITH A FLAT MAIN TIRE
sections.condition: Landing with a flat main tire

items.text: Use Fuel Selector to Reduce Weight on Side of Flat Tire
If Practical, Land with any Crosswind From the Opposite Side of the Flat Tire
Align With the Side of the Runway of the Good Tire
Touchdown Slightly Wing-Low on Side of the Good Tire
Lower Nosewheel Immediately for Directional Control
Hold Airplane Off of Flat Tire for as Long as Possible With Aileron Control

sections.title: LANDING WITH A FLAT NOSE TIRE
sections.condition: Landing with a flat nose tire

items.text: Touchdown on the Center of the Runway

items.response: Full Aft to Minimize Weight on the Nose Wheel
Full Opposite the Direction of the Spin
Retard to LOW RPM Then Set if any Control Available
As Required to Remain Below 2700 RPM

items.text: Land and Close Door Once Aircraft has Come to a Stop
Push Door Open Against Slipstream Then Slam it Closed
Note: A slip in the direction of the open door will assist in latching.
Consult POH for Airspeed & Altitude Corrections
Abandon Aircraft Until All Danger of Fire is Passed
When it is safe to return to the aircraft
ELT is located on right rear bulkhead behind the panel at the rear of the baggage area
Make Periodic Mayday Call and Monitor 121.5 for Instructions
Attempt Contact Using Hand Held Microphone
If Radio Contact Cannot Be Established and is Required (Class B, C, and D Airspace)
Continue Transmissions (Only Receiver May Be Inop)
* Allow circuit breaker to cool 3 minutes before resetting
